tasks.title: A graph that changes its mind
tasks.description: Implement offline dynamic parity connectivity with deletions, including contradictory components. Tested against an independent breadth-first oracle and bounded stress cases.
tasks.prompt: Return JSON {"code": "..."} containing a Python 3.12 module with solve(n, operations). Vertices are 0..n-1. Each operation is ["add",id,u,v,p], ["remove",id], or ["query",u,v]. An active edge asserts color[u] XOR color[v] = p (0 or 1). IDs are unique among active edges and reused only after removal. remove always names an active edge. For every query, return "disconnected" if u and v lie in different connected components; otherwise return "contradiction" if their component has no valid binary coloring; otherwise return their implied XOR as integer 0 or 1. Contradictions elsewhere do not affect this query. n<=20000; at most 60000 operations. Return a list in query order. Inputs are valid. Self edges and parallel edges are permitted. Do not read stdin or execute on import. Standard library only. Aim for near O((n+q) log q) time; recursion limits may be adjusted inside solve.

tasks.title: Snapshot isolation, without write skew
tasks.description: Implement an event-driven transaction engine. Hidden traces target write skew, stale snapshots, read-your-writes, aborted commits, and deletion/recreation.
tasks.prompt: Return JSON {"code":"..."} with a Python 3.12 module defining solve(initial, events). initial maps string keys to integer values. Events are ["begin",tx], ["read",tx,key], ["write",tx,key,value], ["delete",tx,key], ["commit",tx], or ["abort",tx]. Every tx ID is unique; operations only name active transactions; missing keys read as null. begin snapshots the committed database AND per-key version counters. Each key has version 0 initially (including absent keys); every successful commit that writes/deletes a key increments its version, even if the value is unchanged or key was absent. Reads see own pending writes/deletes first, else snapshot. Track all keys explicitly read AND written/deleted. Commit succeeds iff all tracked keys still have their begin-time version; validate even own-write reads. A failed commit discards all writes. A successful commit atomically applies pending writes/deletes. Any commit ends the tx. Abort discards and ends the tx. No predicate/range reads. Return an output entry for each read (value or null) and each commit (boolean), in order; no output for other events. No filesystem, network, or stdin use. Standard library only. At most 10000 events.
